story: The Southern Terminal is a former railway complex at 306 West Depot Avenue. Southern Railway built it in 1903, and architect Frank Pierce Milburn designed both the terminal and the express depot.

It sits in a natural declivity about 15 feet (4.6 m) below the street levels. The railroad changed Knoxville: in the 1850s it helped turn a river town of just over 2,000 people into a major wholesale center.
In 1985 the terminal complex and dozens of nearby warehouses and storefronts were listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

story: Gay Street was part of Charles McClung's original 1791 plat of Knoxville. It has served as the city's main financial and commercial street since the 1790s.

By 1850 it held three-fourths of the city's commercial activity, and in 1854 it became Knoxville's first paved road. On the eve of the Civil War, both Union and Confederate recruiting rallies were held on it at the same time.
After the war the railroad brought an industrial boom. Buildings along the street include the Bijou Theatre (1909), the Riviera Theatre (1920) and the Tennessee Theatre (1928).
stops.fact: In 1854, Gay Street became Knoxville's first paved road.

story: The Blount Mansion was the home of William Blount, the only territorial governor of the Southwest Territory, a signer of the U.S. Constitution and a U.S. senator from Tennessee. It served as the de facto capitol of the territory, and much of the Tennessee Constitution was drafted in his office here in 1796.

The house is a wood-frame home with wood siding, built with materials brought from North Carolina, in a time when most homes in Tennessee were log cabins. Blount lived there with his family and ten enslaved African-American people.

By 1925 the house had deteriorated, and a developer planned to demolish it for a parking lot for the new Andrew Johnson Hotel. A publicity campaign saved it, and the Blount Mansion Association bought it in 1930 and still runs it as a museum.
stops.fact: Blount Mansion was built with materials brought from North Carolina, when most Tennessee homes were log cabins.
stops.disputed: Many people assume old landmarks were always protected. Wikipedia says this one was nearly demolished for a hotel parking lot in 1925.

claims.t: Blount Mansion was built with materials brought from North Carolina.
The mansion was always protected from demolition.

story: The Old Customs House, also called the Old Post Office, was completed in 1874 and was Knoxville's first federal building. It held federal courts, excise offices and the post office until 1933.

It is a three-story Italianate building sheathed in East Tennessee marble, designed by U.S. government chief architect Alfred B. Mullett. As the city's population quadrupled, the building became crowded and was enlarged in 1910.
From 1936 to 1976 it housed Tennessee Valley Authority offices. Since its 2004 expansion it has been home to the East Tennessee History Center.
stops.fact: Knoxville's population quadrupled in the late 19th century, which is why the Customs House was enlarged in 1910.
stops.disputed: Many people picture a quiet small town. Wikipedia says Knoxville's population quadrupled in the late 19th century.

claims.t: The Old Customs House was completed in 1874.
It has always been a history center.
